title: Pure Coordination — chat-allowed variant
description: Identical to pure_coord_01 EXCEPT the `say` verb is transmitted between agents. Same 24×24 meadow, same 5 named landmarks, same agent starting positions, same turn_limit. The only difference is that say messages reach the partner — testing the cross-substrate spatial-convergence hypothesis: if convergence (not communication) is the bottleneck, success rate should remain near 0/N even with the verbal channel open.
goal: Identical to pure_coord_01 (same task, same landmarks, same turn_limit) except the `say` verb IS transmitted to your partner. Both agents see each other's say messages in their event tail. You may verbally negotiate a meeting cell, or stay silent. The win condition is unchanged: end any turn on the SAME (x,y,z) cell as your partner. Reward: +1 to BOTH on first meeting, 0 to BOTH if turn_limit reached without meeting.
notes: Sprint 2 P4 hypothesis-test variant from project_say_cooperation_matrix.md (2026-05-02). Direct disconfirmation experiment for the spatial-convergence hypothesis: if claude-sonnet × claude-sonnet failed pure_coord_01 (silent) at 0/4 because of execution-of-spatial-commitment deficit (NOT communication), then opening the verbal channel should NOT meaningfully improve success rate.
Predicted result if hypothesis correct: ~0/4 still, with say_attempts > 0 (agents will use the channel) but meeting rate similar to pure_coord_01.
Alternative outcome if verbal channel IS the missing piece: ~3-4/4 successes, meaning communication restoration unlocks final convergence.
Either result is paper-grade: the first confirms cross-substrate spatial-convergence finding (n=11 across 4 substrates), the second flips to a richer 'verbal-channel-targeted-spatial-action' framing.

Engine support: `say_filtered: false` is read in initial_state and skips the say-event filter in build_inline_prompt. Default for pure_coord mode is `say_filtered: true` (preserves pure_coord_01 silent behavior).
